rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to elute all 10 compounds if possible and map the overall elution window without risking a truncated run. The wide solvent range and moderate slope should reveal whether retention is concentrated early, late, or across the full gradient.

All compounds eluted comfortably within the gradient, so trim the gradient window to the actual elution region to improve efficiency and reduce run time while keeping similar slope. This should keep all peaks inside the gradient and test whether a focused window can raise CRF by cutting the time term without sacrificing resolution.

The first run already had perfect resolution and the main opportunity is reducing time, so test a steeper version of that successful broad gradient. This will show how much the critical mid-cluster compresses when tG is halved and whether CRF improves through a lower time penalty while staying above the resolution threshold.

The 10 min gradient is fast but over-compresses the critical mid-cluster, while 20 min gives excess resolution; 14 min is a targeted interpolation to recover the 5–7 separations with only a modest time increase. This directly probes the slope sensitivity of the worst pairs and may beat the current CRF if they open enough while the run stays short.

The worst pair improves strongly with a slightly shallower gradient, and 14 min is already close to optimal, so test 16 min to see if pair 6/7 crosses the remaining resolution penalty threshold while keeping the run short enough to preserve a high CRF. This is a focused local refinement around the current best condition.

Slope tuning appears nearly optimized, so now probe temperature to target the stubborn 6/7 pair, which may respond through a modest selectivity shift more than through further tG changes. Lowering T should retain all compounds a bit longer while preserving the successful broad gradient shape.

Lowering temperature worsened selectivity by collapsing peaks 5/6, so test the opposite direction at the best slope. A modest increase to 45 C may shift the critical mid-cluster selectivity favorably while keeping the run short.

Temperature shifts both directions worsened the critical selectivity, so stay at 40 C and test a slightly shallower gradient than 16 min. Since 16 min fully resolved all pairs but incurred only a small time penalty, 18 min will show whether the CRF maximum is truly at 14–16 min or if extra resolution can still be gained efficiently.

The broad 14 min method is near-optimal, so now test a slight trim only at the high-organic end to reduce gradient strength after the last-eluting region while keeping the successful slope and low-organic start. This may preserve the critical mid-cluster spacing yet shorten late elution enough to improve CRF.

A small reduction of phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved the best method, so continue that direction to see if the critical 6/7 pair opens a bit more at essentially no time cost. This is a tight local refinement around the current optimum without changing the successful gradient duration or temperature.

The current best has no time penalty and only a slight resolution shortfall in pair 6/7, so try a modestly steeper gradient at the improved phi1 to probe whether the score benefits from the changed selectivity pattern or if 14 min is truly optimal. This tests whether the narrower high-end window shifts the tG optimum relative to the original 0.95 endpoint.

At phi1 = 0.90, 12 min under-resolves the critical pair while 14 min is excellent, so 16 min tests whether that pair can fully clear with only a small time cost. This is the most informative local check around the current best condition.

With phi1 = 0.90 and tG = 14 min now clearly near-optimal, the only likely path upward is a small selectivity gain for pair 6/7 via temperature. Although 35 C hurt at phi1 = 0.95, the tighter phi window may alter that balance enough to improve the critical pair.

35 C made the mid-cluster worse, so complete the temperature check at the current best phi window by testing 45 C. If neither direction improves selectivity, we can confidently exploit 40 C and focus only on very small phi-window refinements.

Temperature is clearly not the path forward, so probe whether raising phi0 slightly can improve selectivity within the crowded mid-elution region while maintaining the successful upper endpoint. This also checks whether the very early first peak is over-retained relative to the rest and whether a narrower effective window can sharpen the optimum further.

Raising phi0 improved the best method, so combine that gain with the earlier observation that lowering phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 helped. Testing 0.10–0.85 at the same tG and T may further tighten the useful gradient window and push the critical 6/7 pair just a bit farther apart.

We have already reached the maximum CRF, so use a nearby confirmation run to map the local optimum and ensure 0.10–0.85 is not sitting on a broad plateau that might also permit a shorter or more robust method. Lowering phi1 one more step is the cleanest remaining local perturbation around the optimum.

Since lowering phi1 further hurt by stretching the run, the remaining local refinement is to raise phi0 slightly above 0.10 while keeping the optimal upper bound. This tests whether the best point is centered near the early-elution side of the window or if a slightly later start further improves the critical mid-cluster.

We now know the optimum lies on a plateau near phi1 = 0.85 and tG = 14 min, so continue mapping that ridge by increasing phi0 one more step. This checks how far the early end can be raised before the first peak becomes too close to the dead-time region or selectivity in the main cluster starts to degrade.

Two maxima at phi1 = 0.85 suggest a local plateau; testing phi0 = 0.15 with a slightly lower phi1 checks whether that plateau extends diagonally in phi-window space. This is the most informative remaining nearby point because it combines the successful higher phi0 with the only untested adjacent phi1 on that ridge.

The optimum appears to lie on a ridge around phi0 = 0.10–0.15 and phi1 = 0.85, so test the adjacent upper endpoint to complete the local map around the second maximum. This will show whether the 1.000 plateau extends toward higher phi1 or whether 0.85 is the true center.

With the maximum CRF already achieved, use a remaining injection to probe whether a coupled change in slope and temperature can reveal an alternate selectivity regime near the optimum neighborhood. A slightly steeper gradient at lower temperature is the most plausible way to perturb the stubborn 6/7 region without straying far from the proven phi window.

With only a few injections left and the optimum already reached, use one to define the robustness of the 0.15–0.85 window to a shallower slope. This gives a direct comparison against the 14 min maximum and may identify a second fully resolved plateau point with more margin on the critical pair.

Complete the local slope map around one of the optimum methods by testing the corresponding steeper gradient. This brackets the 14 min maximum at the same phi window and confirms how sharply the CRF falls on the fast side.

Use the final run to complete the slope bracketing for the 0.10–0.80 window, since its 14 min result was strong and fully resolved but carried a small time penalty. This final nearby point helps define the local response surface around the proven optimum plateau without risking truncation.
